summary: String-plus-fields reader on a thiscall object. If output buffer a2 is non-null, copies the null-terminated string stored at this+4 into a2, byte by byte including the terminating NUL. If a3 is non-null writes this[68] (offset 0x110) to *a3; if a4 is non-null writes this[69] (offset 0x114) to *a4. Returns a4 as result. All three outputs are optional and gated by null-pointer checks.

local_names.this: source object holding the string buffer and two dword fields
local_names.a2: destination buffer for the string copy
local_names.a3: optional output pointer for the field at offset 0x110
local_names.a4: optional output pointer for the field at offset 0x114; also the return value

operations.description: If a2 is non-null, enter the string-copy path; otherwise skip it entirely.

Copy the null-terminated string at this+4 into a2: iterate a byte cursor v4 from this+4, reading v5 = *v4, writing v5 to the corresponding byte of a2 (v4[a2 - (this+4)] = *v4), advancing v4, and continuing while v5 (the byte just copied) is non-zero so the NUL terminator is also copied.
If a3 is non-null, write the field at offset 0x110 (this[68]) into *a3.
If a4 is non-null, write the field at offset 0x114 (this[69]) into *a4.
Return a4 as the result pointer.
